text:
alex: Heads up converting hf model 'mistral-mini-chat-v2' -> redwood, conversion crashed on final merge step :frowning:

maria: error? paste logs

alex: log:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "convert.py", line 214, in <module>
    merge_weights(shards)
KeyError: 'lm_head.weight'
```
Looks like weight key rename didn't apply — model has `lm_head.weight` but our mapping expects `embed_out.weight`.

kevin: that's odd. the conversion mapping should map `lm_head` -> `embed_out`. did you use the latest keymap?

alex: used redwood-hf-convert v0.9.1 from pip. I also noticed model's config.json uses "tie_word_embeddings": true while our parser expects "tie_embed". suspect config mismatch + safetensors shard index ordering weirdness after a repo re-upload.

sara: also saw hub download flakiness earlier — `curl https://huggingface.co/owner/mistral-mini-chat-v2/resolve/v2/part-0001.safetensors` returned 403 intermittently. revision v2 might have an incomplete LFS push. @ci-bot can you check the last upload status?

ci-bot: last upload for revision v2 completed with warnings: LFS objects failed for 3 files on 2024-11-07 03:12 UTC, retry scheduled. Logs: https://ci.internal/3456/job/789

alex: reproducible locally with:
`redwood-convert --from hf --repo owner/mistral-mini-chat-v2 --revision v2 --out /tmp/mistral-rw`
Fails during weight merge step.

maria: quick workaround: run `python scripts/fix_keys.py /tmp/mistral-rw/weights` to rename keys and then `redwood-load /tmp/mistral-rw` to sanity-check. Example snippet:
```python
# scripts/fix_keys.py (sketch)
import sys, json
from safetensors import safe_open
path = sys.argv[1]
for fname in os.listdir(path):
    with safe_open(os.path.join(path, fname)) as f:
        # map 'lm_head.weight' -> 'embed_out.weight'
        pass
```

kevin: that's fine as a temporary hack but we need two fixes: 1) expand the mapping table to include `lm_head`, `lm_head.weight`, and other aliases; 2) make config parser accept both `tie_word_embeddings` and `tie_embed` keys. I'll open a PR.

alex: FYI evals show a surprising regression after quantizing with our default q4f: +4.7 perplexity on our chat benchmark. Could be missing special tokens or token id shifts — chat templates rely on `<|system|>` but tokenizer.json had a weird escaped newline token.

maria: can you paste the tokenizer special tokens excerpt?

alex: tokenizer.json excerpt:
```json
{"added_tokens":[{"id":50257,"special":true,"content":"\n"}]}
```
The newline got serialized as `\n` and ended up as a token content instead of the expected `<|system|>` id mapping.

sam: this indicates the converter isn't validating special token shapes or raising on unexpected token strings. I'll add a lint step that checks `added_tokens[*].content` against our chat templates and flags mismatches.

kevin: opened PR #1324 — includes keymap aliases, config compatibility, and a hub-download retry that exposes `--allow-lfs` to use HF token for LFS objects. Added unit tests for special token normalization.

alex: thanks. added a short onboarding note: if convert fails with KeyError, check revision re-upload and run `scripts/fix_keys.py` as a stopgap.

maria: tagging support and eng-oncall. @oncall-eng FYI — potential customer impact if someone tries to bring this model up without the patch.

kevin: will backport the patch to v0.9.2 today and cut a hotfix wheel. :hammer_and_wrench:

sara: leaving a note in the model-onboarding checklist to run `redwood-convert --verify` which now (in the patch) checks key aliases and special tokens.

alex: confirmed workaround worked for me — loader now starts and evals run (still investigating q4f regression). Thanks everyone :pray:
